verses.1:1: And it came to pass, when the judges were judging, that a famine arose in the land; and a man departed from Bethlehem of Judah to sojourn in the countryside of Moab, he and his wife and his sons.
verses.1:2: And the name of the man was Abimelech, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites from Bethlehem of Judah; and they came into the countryside of Moab and remained there.
verses.1:3: And Abimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she and her two sons were left behind.
verses.1:4: And they took for themselves Moabite wives; the name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the second was Ruth. And they dwelt there about ten years.
verses.1:5: Then both of them also died, Mahlon and Chilion; and the woman was left bereft of her husband and of her two sons.
verses.1:6: Then she arose, she and her two daughters-in-law, and they returned from the countryside of Moab, for they had heard in the countryside of Moab that the Lord had visited His people to give them bread.
verses.1:7: So she went forth from the place where she had been, and her two daughters-in-law with her; and they walked along the way to return to the land of Judah.
verses.1:8: And Naomi said to her daughters-in-law, "Go now, return each of you to her mother's house. May the Lord show mercy to you, even as you have done with the dead and with me.
verses.1:9: May the Lord grant it to you, and may you find rest, each in the house of her husband." Then she kissed them, and they lifted up their voices and wept.
verses.1:10: And they said to her, "With you we will return to your people."
verses.1:11: But Naomi said, "Turn back now, my daughters; why will you go with me? Are there still sons in my womb, that they should become husbands for you?
verses.1:12: Turn back now, my daughters, for I have grown too old to belong to a husband. Even if I should say that I have hope of belonging to a husband and that I shall bear sons,
verses.1:13: would you wait for them until they are grown? Or would you hold yourselves back for them from belonging to a husband? No indeed, my daughters, for it has become more bitter for me than for you, because the hand of the Lord has gone forth against me."
verses.1:14: And they lifted up their voices and wept again; and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and returned to her people, but Ruth followed her.
verses.1:15: And Naomi said to Ruth, "Behold, your sister-in-law has returned to her people and to her gods; you also turn back now after your sister-in-law."
verses.1:16: But Ruth said, "May it not befall me to forsake you or to turn away from following after you; for wherever you go, I will go, and wherever you abide, I will abide; your people shall be my people, and your God shall be my God.
verses.1:17: And where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. Thus may the Lord do to me, and thus may He add to it, that death alone shall divide between me and you."
verses.1:18: And when Naomi saw that she was steadfastly resolved to go with her, she ceased speaking to her any further.
verses.1:19: So the two of them went on until they arrived at Bethlehem. And all the city was astir with clamor over her, and they said, "Is this Naomi?"
verses.1:20: And she said to them, "Do not call me Naomi; call me Bitter, for the Sufficient One has dealt very bitterly with me.
verses.1:21: I went out full, and the Lord has brought me back empty. Why then do you call me Naomi, when the Lord has humbled me and the Sufficient One has afflicted me?"
verses.1:22: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, returning from the countryside of Moab; and they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.
verses.2:1: Now Naomi had an acquaintance of her husband, a man mighty in strength, of the kindred of Abimelech, and his name was Boaz.
verses.2:2: And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, "Let me go now to the field, and I will gather among the heads of grain after him in whose eyes I may find favor." And she said to her, "Go, daughter."
verses.2:3: So she went and gleaned in the field behind the reapers; and she happened by chance upon the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was of the kindred of Abimelech.
verses.2:4: And behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the reapers, "The Lord be with you." And they said to him, "May the Lord bless you."
verses.2:5: Then Boaz said to his servant who was set over the reapers, "Whose young woman is this?"
verses.2:6: And the servant who was set over the reapers answered and said, "She is the Moabite maiden who returned with Naomi from the countryside of Moab.
verses.2:7: And she said, 'Let me glean now and gather among the sheaves behind the reapers.' So she came and has continued from morning even until evening; she has not rested in the field even a little."
verses.2:8: Then Boaz said to Ruth, "Have you not heard, daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, nor shall you depart from here, but stay close here with my maidens.
verses.2:9: Let your eyes be on the field where they are reaping, and go after them. Behold, I have commanded the young men not to touch you; and whenever you are thirsty, go to the vessels and drink from where the young men draw water."
verses.2:10: Then she fell on her face and bowed down to the ground, and said to him, "Why is it that I have found favor in your eyes, that you should take notice of me, seeing that I am a foreigner?"
verses.2:11: And Boaz answered and said to her, "It has been fully reported to me all that you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband, and how you forsook your father and your mother and the land of your birth, and came to a people whom you did not know yesterday or the day before.
verses.2:12: May the Lord repay your work, and may your reward be full from the Lord, the God of Israel, to whom you have come to trust beneath His wings."
verses.2:13: And she said, "May I find favor in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me, and because you have spoken to the heart of your handmaid; and behold, I shall be as one of your maidservants."
verses.2:14: And Boaz said to her, "It is already the hour to eat; come over here and eat of the bread, and dip your morsel in the vinegar." So Ruth sat beside the reapers, and Boaz heaped up barley meal for her; and she ate and was satisfied, and had some left over.
verses.2:15: And she rose up to glean. And Boaz commanded his young men, saying, "Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not put her to shame.
verses.2:16: Indeed, carry some for her, and also freely cast aside for her from the heaped-up bundles; and she shall eat and glean, and you shall not rebuke her."
verses.2:17: So she gleaned in the field until evening, and beat out what she had gleaned; and it came to about an ephah of barley.
verses.2:18: And she took it up and went into the city; and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. Then Ruth brought out and gave to her what she had left over after she was satisfied.
verses.2:19: And her mother-in-law said to her, "Where did you glean today, and where did you work? Blessed be the one who took notice of you." And Ruth reported to her mother-in-law where she had worked, and said, "The name of the man with whom I worked today is Boaz."
verses.2:20: And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "Blessed is he of the Lord, for He has not forsaken His mercy toward the living and toward the dead." And Naomi said to her, "The man is closely related to us; he is one of our kinsman-redeemers."
verses.2:21: And Ruth said to her mother-in-law, "He also said to me, 'Keep close to my young men until they have finished all the harvest that belongs to me.'"
verses.2:22: And Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "It is good, daughter, that you went with his maidens, and they will not confront you in another field."
verses.2:23: So Ruth kept close to the maidens of Boaz to glean until she finished the harvest of the barley and of the wheat.
verses.3:1: And she dwelt with her mother-in-law. Then Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, "Daughter, shall I not seek rest for you, that it may be well with you?
verses.3:2: And now, is not Boaz our acquaintance, with whose maidens you were? Behold, he is winnowing the threshing floor of barley this night.
verses.3:3: Therefore wash yourself and anoint yourself, and put your apparel upon you, and go up to the threshing floor; do not make yourself known to the man until he has finished drinking and eating.
verses.3:4: And it shall be, when he lies down, that you shall note the place where he lies; and you shall go in and uncover the place at his feet, and lie down; and he will tell you what you shall do."
verses.3:5: And Ruth said to her, "All that you say, I will do."
verses.3:6: So she went down to the threshing floor and did according to all that her mother-in-law had commanded her.
verses.3:7: And Boaz ate, and his heart was glad, and he went to lie down at the side of the heap of grain; and she came secretly and uncovered the place at his feet.
verses.3:8: And it came to pass at midnight that the man was startled and troubled; and behold, a woman was lying at his feet.
verses.3:9: And he said, "Who are you?" And she said, "I am Ruth, your handmaid. Spread the corner of your garment over your handmaid, for you are a kinsman-redeemer."
verses.3:10: Then Boaz said, "Blessed are you of the Lord God, daughter, for you have made your latter kindness better than the first, in not going after the young men, whether poor or rich.
verses.3:11: And now, daughter, do not fear; all that you say I will do for you, for every tribe of my people knows that you are a woman of valor.
verses.3:12: Now it is indeed true that I am a kinsman-redeemer; yet there is a kinsman-redeemer nearer than I.
verses.3:13: Lodge for the night, and it shall be in the morning that if he will redeem you as kinsman, good, let him redeem you; but if he does not wish to redeem you as kinsman, then I will redeem you as kinsman, as the Lord lives—You are the Lord! Lie down until morning."
verses.3:14: So she lay at his feet until morning; and she rose before a man could recognize his neighbor. And Boaz said, "Let it not be known that a woman came to the threshing floor."
verses.3:15: And he said to her, "Bring the mantle that is upon you." And she held it, and he measured out six measures of barley and laid it upon her; and he went into the city.
verses.3:16: And Ruth came to her mother-in-law; and she said to her, "Daughter." And she told her all that the man had done for her.
verses.3:17: And she said to her, "These six measures of barley he gave to me, for he said to me, 'Do not go empty to your mother-in-law.'"
verses.3:18: And she said, "Sit still, daughter, until you know how the matter will not fail; for the man will surely not rest until he completes the matter today."
verses.4:1: Now Boaz went up to the gate and sat down there; and behold, the kinsman-redeemer of whom Boaz had spoken was passing by. And Boaz said to him, "Turn aside and sit down here, O hidden one." So he turned aside and sat down.
verses.4:2: And Boaz took ten men from the elders of the city and said, "Sit down here." So they sat down.
verses.4:3: And Boaz said to the kinsman-redeemer, "The portion of the field that belongs to our brother Abimelech, which has been given to Naomi, who has returned from the country of Moab—
verses.4:4: I also said, 'I will uncover your ear, saying: Acquire it in the presence of those sitting here and in the presence of the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, redeem it; but if you will not redeem it, declare it to me, and I shall know, for there is no one besides you to redeem it, and I am after you.'" And he said, "I am he; I will redeem it."
verses.4:5: Then Boaz said, "On the day you acquire the field from the hand of Naomi and from Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead man, you must also acquire her, so as to raise up the name of the dead man upon his inheritance."
verses.4:6: And the kinsman-redeemer said, "I will not be able to redeem it for myself, lest I ruin my own inheritance. Redeem for yourself my right of redemption, for I will not be able to redeem it."
verses.4:7: Now this was the ordinance in former times in Israel concerning the right of redemption and concerning exchange, to confirm every matter: a man would take off his sandal and give it to his neighbor who was redeeming his right of redemption; and this was a testimony in Israel.
verses.4:8: So the kinsman-redeemer said to Boaz, "Acquire for yourself my right of redemption." And he took off his sandal and gave it to him.
verses.4:9: And Boaz said to the elders and to all the people, "You are witnesses this day that I have acquired all that belongs to Abimelech, and all that belongs to Chilion and to Mahlon, from the hand of Naomi;
verses.4:10: moreover, Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, I have acquired for myself as a wife, to raise up the name of the dead man upon his inheritance, and the name of the dead man shall not be cut off from among his brethren and from the tribe of his people. You are witnesses this day."
verses.4:11: And all the people who were at the gate said, "We are witnesses." And the elders said, "May the Lord make your wife, who is entering into your house, like Rachel and like Leah, who both built the house of Israel and did valiantly in Ephrathah; and there shall be a name in Bethlehem;
verses.4:12: and may your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, from the seed that the Lord shall give you by this young woman."
verses.4:13: And Boaz took Ruth, and the Lord gave her conception, and she bore a son.
verses.4:14: And the women said to Naomi, "Blessed be the Lord, who has not taken away from you a kinsman-redeemer this day, so as to proclaim your name in Israel;
verses.4:15: and he shall be to you one who restores the soul and sustains your gray hair; for your daughter-in-law, who has loved you, has borne him—she who is better to you than seven sons."
verses.4:16: And Naomi took the child and laid him in her bosom, and she became a nurse to him.
verses.4:17: And the neighbor women gave him a name, saying, "A son has been born to Naomi." And they called his name Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
verses.4:18: Now these are the generations of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron,
verses.4:19: and Hezron fathered Arran, and Arran fathered Amminadab,
verses.4:20: and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon,
verses.4:21: and Salmon fathered Boaz, and Boaz fathered Obed,
verses.4:22: and Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.

notes.1:2: The Greek text reads Abimelech (matching 1:3, 2:1, 2:3) rather than the Hebrew Elimelech, and does not mention Naomi's name until 1:3.
notes.1:14: The Greek includes "and returned to her people" and renders Ruth's action as "followed her" rather than the Hebrew "clung to her."
notes.1:16: The Greek renders Ruth's opening plea as an optative wish, "May it not befall me to forsake you," reflecting a distinct reading of the Hebrew verb.
notes.1:20: The Greek translates the name Mara as "Bitter" (Pikran) and renders Hebrew Shaddai as "the Sufficient One" (ho hikanos, also in 1:21).
notes.2:7: The Greek reads "from morning even until evening; she has not rested in the field even a little," resolving a difficult clause in the Hebrew text.
notes.2:13: Unlike the Hebrew ("though I am not like one of your maidservants"), the Greek lacks a negation and reads positively, "and behold, I shall be as one of your maidservants."
notes.2:16: The Greek preserves a fuller command from Boaz, adding "carry some for her" and "she shall eat and glean."
notes.3:1: Following the Septuagint verse division, the sentence "And she dwelt with her mother-in-law" opens 3:1 rather than closing 2:23.
notes.3:13: The Greek text preserves the striking exclamation "as the Lord lives—You are the Lord!" (ze Kyrios, sy ei Kyrios) in Boaz's oath.
notes.3:16: The Greek gives Naomi's greeting simply as "Daughter," without the Hebrew question "Who are you, my daughter?"
notes.3:18: The Greek includes a negation ("how the matter will not fail," literally "will not fall"), expressing confidence that the matter will not come to nothing.
notes.4:1: The Greek vocative κρύφιε ("hidden one") renders the Hebrew idiom for an unnamed person literally as one whose name is concealed.
notes.4:3: The Septuagint reads "Abimelech" (also in v. 9) rather than Hebrew "Elimelech," and reads the passive "which has been given to Naomi" rather than "is selling."
notes.4:10: The Septuagint reads "from the tribe of his people" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "from the gate of his place"; in v. 9 the Greek also reverses the order of the brothers to "Chilion and Mahlon."
notes.4:14: The Septuagint reads "your name" (referring to Naomi) rather than Hebrew "his name," and uses the active form καλέσαι ("to proclaim").
notes.4:19: The Septuagint genealogy reads "Arran" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Ram."
